quality_effect: Make EA LiDAR point-density, datum/version and independent ground-truth limits explicit before numeric elevation promotion.

official_sources.title: Survey Data Catalogue - point density considered in the LiDAR programme

verified_facts: Ground-truth elevation points are independently surveyed to verify EA time-stamped LiDAR.
Ground-truth attributes include survey date, surface type, survey method, transformation and geoidal model.
Ground-truth surveys generally must be less than 5 years old, or 3 years for coastal projects, for reuse.
EA LiDAR surveys must be below +/-15cm RMSE to pass quality control.
EA also requires standard deviation and random error below 10cm for QC.
A 1m DSM survey has an average point density of at least 1 point per square metre.
50cm DSM corresponds to at least 4 points per square metre and 25cm to 16 points per square metre.
Point density describes point clouds and is not the same as raster resolution.
Under vegetation, DTM point density may be lower than DSM point density.
EA data are supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
Time-stamped and point-cloud products require the metadata catalogue to identify the specific geoid model used for a survey.
